audits.title: Completion rate to caecum as a quality measure of colonoscopy in a district general hospital.
audits.setting: District general hospital endoscopy unit (Wycombe Hospital)

cycle1.result: Unit completion rate 89.1% (95% CI 87-92%); individuals ranged 75% to 97%.

audits.intervention: Working practices altered for endoscopists not meeting the target

cycle2.result: Trend towards improvement in those individuals.

audits.other_findings: Trainees needed at least 40 procedures to reach 85% completion; colorectal cancer detected in 3.9%.
audits.citation: Gorard DA, McIntyre AS. Completion rate to caecum as a quality measure of colonoscopy in a district general hospital. Colorectal Dis. 2004;6(4):243-249. doi:10.1111/j.1463-1318.2004.00628.x. PMID: 15206966.

audits.title: Quality improvement programme to achieve acceptable colonoscopy completion rates: prospective before and after study.
audits.setting: Endoscopy department, North Tyneside General Hospital
audits.intervention: Longer appointments, admitting frail patients to one ward for bowel preparation, and allocating colonoscopies to the most successful operators.
audits.other_findings: Completion rate was 71% after the first audit round; failures were due to lack of time, poor bowel preparation and operator mismatch.
audits.citation: Ball JE, Osbourne J, Jowett S, Pellen M, Welfare MR. Quality improvement programme to achieve acceptable colonoscopy completion rates: prospective before and after study. BMJ. 2004;329(7467):665-667. doi:10.1136/bmj.329.7467.665. PMID: 15374917.

audits.title: Prospective audit of colonoscopy quality in Kent and Medway, UK.
audits.standard: National standards: total colonoscopy in at least 90%; BSG sedation guidelines; more than 100 colonoscopies per year
audits.setting: 7 endoscopy units, Kent and Medway Strategic Health Authority

cycle1.result: 39 of 55 colonoscopists (71%) achieved total colonoscopy in at least 90%; 12 (22%) in 80-89%; 4 (7%) in 79% or less; 79% sedated per BSG guidelines; 22 of 55 (40%) performed more than 100 colonoscopies.

audits.other_findings: Complications below expected levels; seven doctors stopped performing colonoscopy during the study.
audits.citation: Taylor KM, Arajs K, Rouse T, Harris AW. Prospective audit of colonoscopy quality in Kent and Medway, UK. Endoscopy. 2008;40(4):291-295. doi:10.1055/s-2007-995528. PMID: 18389447.

audits.title: Three consecutive audits to achieve acceptable colonoscopy completion rates.
audits.setting: Endoscopy unit, Medical Unit One, Civil Hospital Karachi

cycle1.result: Crude caecal intubation rate 55%; adjusted rate not calculable due to inadequate documentation.

audits.intervention: Proforma introduced for prospective data collection and further improvements in methodology after each audit.
audits.other_findings: Second audit (December 2005 to November 2006, n = 119): crude 54.8%, adjusted 75%.
audits.citation: Bhatty SA, Shaikh NA, Akhter SS, Manzoor H, Khatian A, Khan B, et al.. Three consecutive audits to achieve acceptable colonoscopy completion rates. J Pak Med Assoc. 2009;59(7):461-463. PMID: 19579735.

audits.title: Scope to improve: a multi-centre audit of 16 064 colonoscopies looking at caecal intubation rates, over a 2-year period.
audits.standard: JAG quality standard: caecal intubation rate 90% and 100+ colonoscopies per operator per annum
audits.setting: Six hospitals across three English regions

cycle1.result: Overall caecal intubation rate 90.57% (95% CI 90.11% to 91.01%); operators doing 100+ procedures per annum 91.76%.

audits.other_findings: Low-volume endoscopists (<100 per annum) had CIR below 90%, and non-screening colonoscopists performed worse than BCSP colonoscopists.
audits.citation: Verma AM, McGrath N, Bennett P, de Caestecker J, Dixon A, Eaden J, et al.. Scope to improve: a multi-centre audit of 16 064 colonoscopies looking at caecal intubation rates, over a 2-year period. Frontline Gastroenterol. 2012;3(3):124-129. doi:10.1136/flgastro-2012-100118. PMID: 28839652.
